subject: Post-call: Performance SLO (p95/p99) qualification — hosted API vs current provider
messages:
From: Laura Bennett <laura@redwood.com>
To: Samir Shah <samir@finlytics.com>
Cc: Priya Joshi <p.joshi@finlytics.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 18 Dec 2026 15:10:00 -0800
Subject: Post-call recap & next steps — Performance SLOs (p95/p99)

Thanks again for the call today, Samir — really helpful to see the FinLytics production traffic profile. Quick recap and proposed next steps.

Recap:
- Primary constraint: end-to-end inference latency for "insight generation" flow (single user request -> streamed tokens back to client).
- Target SLOs you mentioned: p95 <= 250ms, p99 <= 800ms end-to-end across your EU+US user base.
- Typical request size: median 120 tokens, 95th token-length ~650 tokens.
- Concurrency: steady-state ~120 concurrent requests, peak bursts to ~350 concurrent.
- Streaming: SSE-based streaming to end-client required for UX (token-by-token).

What we need from you (next steps):
1) Can you share a redacted example trace (end-to-end) for a p95 and p99 request — headers/timings for client->app->provider->response? You mentioned you could export traces — attachment stub would be perfect.
2) Confirm which percent of traffic requires 1:1 session persistence (KV cache warm) vs pure stateless inference.
3) Any contractual hard stop on p99 (e.g., penalty / SLA requirement)?

What we can deliver quickly:
- Marissa will run a short-hosted API microbenchmark against a representative model and replay of your traces (if you share) to compare p95/p99 numbers and streaming behavior.
- We'll produce a short 1-pager mapping your requirements to Hosted API configuration options (batching, streaming buffer, concurrency limits, region routing).

Proposed timeline:
- You provide traces & confirmation on session persistence by EOD Mon (12/21).
- We run replay + short report by Wed (12/23).

Attachments: none yet — please attach the traces when you have them.

Thanks — laura

Laura — thanks for the recap. Attaching the traces and a small SLO matrix we keep internally. Two quick clarifications:

- The p95/p99 numbers I quoted are what product owners expect at the CDN edge (end-to-end from browser to rendered token). We understand some variance is from network, but we're trying to set realistic provider-level targets so that total E2E meets p95/p99 goals.
- Session persistence: ~65% of traffic is interactive (session with KV warm). The rest is stateless batch calls.

Subject: Fwd: Post-call recap & next steps — Performance SLOs (p95/p99)

Marissa / Aditya — forwarding traces Samir sent (attached). High level asks: can Hosted API meet FinLytics' end-to-end p95 <= 250ms, p99 <= 800ms targets for interactive sessions at their steady-state concurrency (~120) and burst (~350)? They require streaming (SSE) semantics and ~65% session-persistent calls.

Please run a replay of the traces on a representative model (they use an open LLM variant similar to redwood/fast-13b) and produce:
- Observed p50/p95/p99 end-to-end latencies on Hosted API default config (no special batching).
- Observed p50/p95/p99 with recommended batching and streaming buffer tweaks.
- Notes on KV warm-up effect (first request vs warmed).
- Any recommendations on autoscale config to handle 350 concurrent bursts without p99 spikes.

Timeline: if you can get an initial datapoint by Wed (12/23) that would be ideal — Samir is flexible for a follow-up on Thurs.

Thanks — laura

From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
To: Samir Shah <samir@finlytics.com>, Laura Bennett <laura@redwood.com>
Cc: Aditya Rao <aditya@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 24 Dec 2026 09:22:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Post-call recap & next steps — Performance SLOs (p95/p99)

Samir / Team — quick update from the replay we ran against the traces you provided. We used a hosted instance in us-west with model config matching your description (open-13b-like), replayed the trace with both stateless and session-warm flows, and measured end-to-end timings including streaming output. High-level results below — attaching a short runbook (redwood-hosted-latency-runbook.pdf) with config used.

Observed (hosted API, baseline settings):
- steady-state concurrency 120 (65% warm sessions): p50 = 110ms, p95 = 280ms, p99 = 750ms
- burst concurrency 350 (simulated ramp): p50 = 130ms, p95 = 420ms, p99 = 1.1s

With recommended tuning (aggressive batching, 20ms streaming buffer, prioritized session routing):
- steady-state 120: p50 = 95ms, p95 = 210ms, p99 = 540ms
- burst 350: p50 = 115ms, p95 = 300ms, p99 = 780ms

Notes / recommendations:
- For p99 stability under burst, we recommend a small dedicated pool for interactive sessions (session pinning) to avoid cold KV impact and to limit cross-tenant queueing. That reduces p99 by ~30-40% in our replay.
- Enable regional routing (us + eu) to reduce network variance for EU users; we saw ~70ms median network delta for EU->US in the traces.
- If FinLytics needs hard p99 contractual guarantees <= 800ms for bursts, we should pair a reserved Dedicated pool (or dedicated capacity for interactive sessions) with Hosted routing for non-interactive traffic.

Next steps:
- If you want, we can provision a short trial with a dedicated interactive pool to run your workload for 24-72 hours and capture production-like metrics.
- I'll schedule a 30-min follow-up demo to walk through the runbook and sample metrics — Thu or Fri next week?

Attachments: redwood-hosted-latency-runbook.pdf

Best —
